privacy.notice: Your cycle logs stay on your phone. You choose what to share.

flag.none.v1.title: Cycle Pattern Within Personal Baseline
flag.none.v1.summary: Your cycle timing, flow, and symptoms remain consistent with your personal baseline.
flag.none.v1.meaning: No unusual shift or drift was observed across your recent cycle logs based on your personal historical range.
flag.none.v1.next_steps: Keep logging your cycles to maintain your personalized baseline. If you feel unwell or notice changes, consider consulting a doctor.
flag.none.v1.doctor_consult: If you experience any new discomfort or have health questions, consider consulting a doctor.

flag.irregularity.v1.title: Cycle Length Variation Observed
flag.irregularity.v1.summary: Your cycle length differed noticeably from your usual personal rhythm.
flag.irregularity.v1.meaning: Your cycle was longer or shorter than what is typical for you. Temporary variations often happen with travel, changes in sleep, or acute stress.
flag.irregularity.v1.next_steps: Continue recording your dates over the next two to three cycles. If irregular intervals persist, consider consulting a doctor.
flag.irregularity.v1.doctor_consult: For recurring irregular cycles, consider consulting a doctor.

flag.pcos_pattern.v1.title: PCOS-Like Screening Pattern
flag.pcos_pattern.v1.summary: Your cycles have been longer than usual for a few months, and you noted some other changes.
flag.pcos_pattern.v1.meaning: This screening flag reflects a combination of lengthened cycles alongside signals like skin breakouts or hair changes. This is a risk pattern sometimes associated with polycystic ovary syndrome, but this screening flag does not mean you have it. A doctor can check with simple tests.
flag.pcos_pattern.v1.next_steps: Keep a steady record of your symptoms and cycle timing. A healthcare professional can evaluate your overall health with routine clinical checks.
flag.pcos_pattern.v1.doctor_consult: To evaluate these hormonal patterns accurately, consider consulting a doctor.

flag.anemia_pattern.v1.title: Anemia-Like Screening Pattern
flag.anemia_pattern.v1.summary: Heavier menstrual flow combined with elevated tiredness matches an iron deficiency risk pattern.
flag.anemia_pattern.v1.meaning: Substantial menstrual blood loss alongside dizziness or fatigue suggests your iron reserves may be depleted.
flag.anemia_pattern.v1.next_steps: Prioritize nourishing, iron-rich meals like lentils, leafy greens, and jaggery. Take rest when feeling low on energy.
flag.anemia_pattern.v1.doctor_consult: If heavy bleeding or weakness continues across cycles, consider consulting a doctor for a routine blood count.

flag.thyroid_pattern.v1.title: Thyroid-Like Screening Pattern
flag.thyroid_pattern.v1.summary: Shifts in your cycle length together with fatigue or weight changes match a thyroid risk pattern.
flag.thyroid_pattern.v1.meaning: Thyroid hormone balance influences metabolic rate and menstrual timing. A noticeable cycle shift accompanied by sustained fatigue or weight changes is an indicator worth reviewing.
flag.thyroid_pattern.v1.next_steps: Note any additional sensations such as temperature sensitivity or mood shifts. Routine lab tests can easily assess thyroid function.
flag.thyroid_pattern.v1.doctor_consult: To review these metabolic and menstrual patterns, consider consulting a doctor.

confidence.low: Low confidence: based on limited cycle history.
confidence.medium: Medium confidence: consistent signal across recent cycles.
confidence.high: High confidence: multiple corroborating signals persisted over multiple cycles.

signals.cycle_length_high: Cycle length noticeably longer than your baseline
signals.cycle_length_low: Cycle length noticeably shorter than your baseline
signals.flow_high: Menstrual flow noticeably heavier than usual
signals.pain_high: Period discomfort higher than your personal typical level
